findings.problem: The end of the proof makes a round trip. First `rw [hl,hr] at h` turns the refined sums `∑ k ∈ s.product t, r k.1 • (e k.1*f k.2)` in `h` into the coarse sums `∑ i ∈ s, r i • e i`. Then `←H (fun k => r k.1)` and `←H (fun k => v k.2)` bring the refined sums back, and a second `hl,hr` turns them coarse again. So `hl` and `hr` are each applied twice, in the same direction but at different stages. That hides the simple plan: rewrite the goal once in terms of the refined partition, then use linearity of `quotientValue` on that partition.
findings.proposed_change:
Keep lines 67–76 as they are. Replace lines 77–78 with a single goal rewrite:
```lean
  rw [← hl, ← hr, h, H (fun k => r k.1), H (fun k => v k.2)]
```
After `← hl, ← hr`, the goal reads `qV(∑ r k.1 • ef + ∑ v k.2 • ef) = qV(∑ r k.1 • ef) + qV(∑ v k.2 • ef)`. Here `qV` stands for `T.quotientValue hadd hsqrt` and `ef` for `e k.1 * f k.2`. `h` rewrites the left side to `∑ ↑(r k.1) * qV ef + ∑ ↑(v k.2) * qV ef`. The two forward uses of `H` rewrite the right side to the same expression, so `rw` closes the goal by `rfl`. Each rewrite uses only terms that already appear in rewrites that succeed in the current proof.
findings.benefit: Each fact is now used once and in one direction. Lifting both sides to the refined partition `e k.1 * f k.2` is the core idea of the lemma. The reader can then see that the left side is handled by the combined weighting `h` and each right-hand summand by `H`, without following a back-and-forth with `hl`/`hr`. The proof loses one line and one `at h` rewrite and uses no new lemmas or automation.
